transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (CopperPoint Cloud), Rajiv (Head of Infra), Hannah (Security Lead), Owen (SRE), Jess (Procurement)

Summary: quick intake — customer evaluating Private deployment (VPC onramp) for regulated workloads. They want network design options, region gating, and compliance artifacts.

--- Transcript body (auto-generated, imperfect) ---
00:00:03 Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick round of intros?
00:00:10 Maya (CopperPoint): Hi all, Maya here, cloud architect, I'll be owning the network side.
00:00:14 Rajiv (CopperPoint): Rajiv, infra. We're trying to figure out how Redwood would fit with our VPC topology.
00:00:18 Elena (Redwood): Great. High-level we'll cover the private options, peering patterns, egress, and any region constraints. Feel free to interrupt.
00:00:28 Owen (CopperPoint): FYI, we have a strict egress policy — only specific IP ranges allowed outbound.
00:00:33 Samir (Redwood): Makes sense, we'll talk egress ranges and static IPs. First question — are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or full private?
00:00:42 Rajiv (CopperPoint): We want private. Data residency and audit controls mean hosted API is meh for now. But we need to understand the networking patterns — do you support VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink?
00:00:55 Diego (Redwood): All three patterns are supported, with tradeoffs. VPC peering is simplest but doesn't scale cross-account easily for many VPCs. Transit gateway is our recommended for hub-and-spoke at scale. PrivateLink (Private Endpoints) is preferred for direct service endpoints without route table changes.
00:01:16 Hannah (CopperPoint): For compliance we need explicit egress control, audit logs, and KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed keys?
00:01:24 Elena (Redwood): Yes, Private supports KMS integrations and in on-prem cases HSM options. We need to coordinate key policy and rotation. We'll send our KMS integration doc.
00:01:35 Maya (CopperPoint): Regions — we process EU customer data, must keep model inference in eu-west-1. Do you have an offering there?
00:01:42 Samir (Redwood): We support deployments in eu-west-1 for Private, but availability varies by model. We'll include a model/region compatibility matrix.
00:01:52 Rajiv (CopperPoint): Networking specifics — can you advertise routes to our TGW or do we need peering?
00:01:58 Diego (Redwood): For Transit Gateway, Redwood's Private nodes can attach via a customer-managed TGW peering and we support route propagation; for peering we exchange route tables. For PrivateLink we provision an interface endpoint in your VPC and you control the SGs.
00:02:15 Owen (CopperPoint): Latency — we need <60ms p95 for text-generation at 512 tokens. Will that hold if model sits in another region?
00:02:24 Elena (Redwood): Latency depends on region and model. For EU data residency you should colocate inference nodes in eu-west-1; that achieves lowest latency. If you route to a different region there will be extra inter-region latency. We can run a simple ping + sample inference benchmark during the next workshop.
00:02:43 Maya (CopperPoint): Egress IPs — we enforce firewall allow-lists. Can you provide stable egress addresses?
00:02:49 Samir (Redwood): For Private we give static egress IP blocks for customer deployments; we'll provide a spreadsheet of IP ranges. For hosted they vary, but Dedicated/Private can be fixed.
00:02:59 Hannah (CopperPoint): What about logging and audit trails? Need to show per-request logs (redaction allowed) and retention window options.
00:03:07 Diego (Redwood): We stream audit logs to your S3/Kafka or push them into your SIEM. Retention is configurable in the Private control plane. Also request-level traces can be sampled.
00:03:20 Rajiv (CopperPoint): Network ACLs — do you require open ports? What's the minimal firewall footprint?
00:03:25 Elena (Redwood): Minimal: outbound to our control plane for provisioning (HTTPS), and either interface endpoints for PrivateLink or peering routes for TGW/peering. We'll document exact ports.
00:03:40 Jess (CopperPoint): Procurement note — we'll need standard contract, also any third-party subprocessor list.
00:03:46 Samir (Redwood): We'll include subprocessor list and contract template in the pack.
00:03:51 Hannah (CopperPoint): Does Redwood do in-cluster model hosting or is it a sidecar?
00:03:56 Diego (Redwood): For Private it's our runtime in customer VPC or connected via private network; it runs on dedicated instances managed by the customer or on Redwood-managed nodes depending on the engagement. There are on-prem options.
00:04:10 Rajiv (CopperPoint): If we bring our own GPUs on-prem, do you have an operator?
00:04:15 Elena (Redwood): We provide an on-prem package with an orchestrator and control plane; conjunction with HSM is possible but more of an enterprise engagement.
00:04:28 Maya (CopperPoint): Any gotchas about CIDR overlap? We're VPC space limited.
00:04:32 Diego (Redwood): CIDR overlap is the usual pain point. PrivateLink avoids it (uses ENIs), TGW requires non-overlapping routes for propagation. We'll propose NAT + proxy patterns if overlap exists.
00:04:49 Owen (CopperPoint): Are you able to scale autoscaling pools? We might see bursts during batch processing at month-end.
00:04:56 Elena (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated/Private platforms support configurable autoscaling with burst capacity. We can set policies by queue depth and request latency.
00:05:10 Rajiv (CopperPoint): What about model variants for cost control? Quantization?
00:05:15 Diego (Redwood): Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles and will recommend smaller variants; runtime supports int8 quantized kernels. We'll share recommended profiles for common workloads.
00:05:28 Hannah (CopperPoint): Security architecture — SSO, RBAC, SAML?
00:05:33 Samir (Redwood): SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, role-based access, audit logs per token. For Private we can integrate with your IdP.
00:05:45 Maya (CopperPoint): Can we get flow diagram examples?
00:05:48 Elena (Redwood): Yes, Diego will attach diagrams (TGW, peering, PrivateLink).
00:05:52 Rajiv (CopperPoint): Bandwidth costs — if inference nodes are remote, egress costs add up.
00:05:58 Samir (Redwood): Correct; colocating in same region reduces egress; we'll include cost estimates in the pricing worksheet.
00:06:08 Jess (CopperPoint): Timeline — target pilot in Q1 2027. We need security sign-off before procurement.
00:06:14 Samir (Redwood): Good, we'll aim to have deliverables in the next two weeks to support that timeline.

(15:00–45:00 Discussion deep dives and clarifications, timestamps intermittently present)

00:18:02 Hannah (CopperPoint): A quick nit — for audit logs, we need logs to be immutable for 7 years. Can you support long-term retention and WORM?
00:18:10 Diego (Redwood): We can export to your S3 with object lock for WORM; retention policies can be set on your side.
00:24:58 Rajiv (CopperPoint): For the private endpoint option, do you provision the ENI in our account or we do?
00:25:05 Elena (Redwood): Typically the endpoint is created in your account/VPC and you attach our service via service name; we provide CloudFormation/Terraform templates to simplify.
00:31:40 Maya (CopperPoint): Does Redwood require inbound security allowances from our side?
00:31:44 Samir (Redwood): Only for management plane if you choose a control plane that needs access; otherwise it's mostly outbound from your VPC to Redwood-managed control plane endpoints over TLS.
00:36:12 Owen (CopperPoint): Can you show an example of the egress IP block we can use for allow-listing?
00:36:18 Diego (Redwood): We'll include an alpha spreadsheet with /24 blocks for the pilot; final blocks depend on the deployment sizing.
00:42:00 Rajiv (CopperPoint): If we want to run everything strictly in eu-west-1 with customer-managed keys, any blockers?
00:42:07 Elena (Redwood): No blockers, we'll validate the model's availability in region; for CMK we need cross-account key policy that permits Redwood services; we'll follow your security team's process.
00:49:30 Jess (CopperPoint): Procurement will need SLAs and incident response times.
00:49:34 Samir (Redwood): We'll provide SLA docs and standard incident response playbooks.
00:52:10 Samir (Redwood): Ok, quick recap — Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, subprocessor list), network diagrams (TGW/peering/PrivateLink), IP ranges spreadsheet, Dedicated vs Private pricing, and propose times for a 2-hour network deep-dive workshop. CopperPoint to share VPC CIDRs, egress policy, and confirm KMS requirements.
00:52:40 Maya (CopperPoint): Sounds good.
00:52:47 Hannah (CopperPoint): We'll also loop legal for contract terms.
00:52:51 Samir (Redwood): Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs and the calendar invite.
00:52:58 Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and missing punctuation common to auto transcripts. References to specific product names (PrivateLink, Transit Gateway) may have slight naming differences in our docs.
